description: Exact bounded minimum-cardinality arc deletion to make a directed graph acyclic, using a vertex-order subset DP.

source.title: A Note on Exact Algorithms for Vertex Ordering Problems on Graphs
source.authors: Hans L. Bodlaender, Fedor V. Fomin, Arie M. C. A. Koster, Dieter Kratsch, and Dimitrios M. Thilikos
source.primary_reference: Section 3 additive Held–Karp-style subset DP; Section 5.7 Lemma 9 equates minimum directed feedback arc set with minimum backward-arc ordering.
source.copyright: The publication is used as an algorithmic reference only; this package is clean-room authored.

input.graph: Simple directed graph without loops. Each ordered arc occurs at most once; antiparallel arcs are allowed and count separately.

output.meaning: Minimum number of directed arcs whose deletion makes the graph acyclic.

algorithm_details.primary: Let dp[S] be the minimum backward-arc count for an ordering of prefix vertex set S. Appending v costs the number of arcs v->u with u in S, so dp[S union {v}] = min(dp[S union {v}], dp[S] + outdegree(v,S)). Iterate masks and vertices in ascending order; equal-cost updates keep the first predecessor. Complexity O(N^2*2^N) time and O(2^N) states.
algorithm_details.independent_oracle: Enumerate every permutation, build the position of each vertex, count input arcs (u,v) with position[u] > position[v], and return the minimum. This directly checks the ordering objective rather than subset transitions.
algorithm_details.tie_rules: Vertices are considered in ascending ID order and masks in ascending numeric order. Only the minimum cost is returned, so equal-cost orderings are observationally equivalent.
algorithm_details.arithmetic_bound: A simple loopless digraph on eight vertices has at most 56 arcs. For any order, each unordered vertex pair contributes at most one backward arc, so the result is at most 28; all intermediate costs fit signed 64-bit arithmetic.
